column1: # tests/budgets.tsv (W160): every `make test-long` command, its wall-time budget in
# seconds at EFS_TEST_JOBS=8 on an 8-CPU host with one NVMe (1.25 x the nuc run of
# Oct 25), the pool slots it occupies while it runs, and, for a budget above the bound
# in tests/test_make_test_recipe.py, why. Slots weigh disk use, not CPU (the daemon
# tests use 0.15-0.3 CPU each but their stores fsync on one disk): 6 the report
# step-down test, whose 3 s latency bound needs a quiet disk (it starts first; D4, whose
# packer PUT deadlines need the same, is the first two-slot command and runs beside
# it); 3 a test whose driver or writers fsync for most of its run (B growth, stop
# progress), so at most two overlap; 2 a daemon test that writes a moderate set with fsync;
# 1 a test that mostly waits on daemon timers (member-down detection, unmount fences,
# the slow member's deliberate delays) or a CPU-bound process. scripts/make_test_summary.sh starts the
# largest budgets first and lists OVERBUDGET commands; tests/test_make_test_recipe.py
# bounds the budgets and the budgeted gate time. Evidence: docs/status/gate-speed-20261025.md.

column4: one cluster carries additions, a restart and five outages in sequence; its writer is paced to two files a second, so it is a two-slot command that runs beside the report step-down test once D4 is done
seven steps on one cluster: two waits on the 30 s member-down detection, nine unmounts with a member down (15 s storage fence each)

three members with the B1-B5 driver and B2 on the stores, then four and five with the driver (fsync writes and read-backs of about 500 files per size; 58 s alone, up to three times that beside other writers)
a fresh cluster grown to five, then six to eight members with the B1-B5 driver at every size (84 s alone, up to three times that beside other writers)
1,500 directories and files through FUSE, then the stop steps (66 s alone, up to four times that beside other writers)
deliberate slow-member delays (8 s per operation, 45 s reads, 65 s commit) past the client deadlines
bounded-progress gate (76-125 s; packer PUT deadlines fail beside fsync-heavy tests): the budget above every other two-slot command makes it the first, in the report step-down window

asserts a 3 s bound on every append and fsync through three metadata step-downs (1,600 appends, 200 fsyncs; 265-350 s on the nuc): six slots, so it starts first and only D4 and then timer-bound tests run beside it; an fsync-heavy neighbour breaks the bound

the four-member expiry fixture and its fsynced create bursts (135 s alone, 133-262 s in the pool depending on its neighbours): three slots and a budget below D4's, so it never runs beside the report step-down or D4 in the first wave
Three private loopback daemons: refusal, ReadIndex, CREATE and orderly stop
